+# ADR-001 — Volunteer identity provider
+
+## Context
+
+PRD-001 explicitly requests an identity-provider ADR for FR-001. It specifies
+browser sign-in but no provider, existing tenant, email access, credential method,
+or enrollment/recovery process. Smartphone access alone does not resolve these.
+
+## Proposed direction and alternatives
+
+Use a hosted identity service behind a server-side adapter, with local application
+sessions and roles as specified in [ADD-001](../add/ADD-001.md). Prefer an existing
+compatible hosted identity tenant if one exists; otherwise evaluate a managed
+provider with a browser redirect protocol such as OIDC. No particular provider
+or login method has been selected or validated.
+
+| Option | Benefit | Limitation |
+|---|---|---|
+| Existing hosted organization identity | May reuse account operations | No tenant or volunteer eligibility is established |
+| New managed identity provider | Moves credential lifecycle to a hosted service | Requires usable enrollment/recovery, cost and operational fit to be established |
+| Application-owned credentials or custom magic links | Direct control of login experience | Adds credential/recovery/delivery responsibilities; not justified for this pilot |
+
+The application must not depend on provider-wide logout timing to meet NFR-001.
+Identity proves who signed in; the local session gate decides whether a request
+is still authorized. Phone numbers stay out of identity claims and profiles.
+
+## Resolution evidence
+
+The implementation owner, with product-owner input on volunteer access, records:
+
+1. Selected provider and supported volunteer/staff credential method, enrollment,
+   account recovery, and stable external identity mapping. Establish whether an
+   existing tenant can serve these users; do not assume email or SMS availability.
+2. Current official provider documentation and a hosted callback proof showing
+   valid sign-in, rejection of invalid/replayed responses, and safe account mapping.
+3. A two-browser demonstration that local revocation rejects old application
+   sessions independently of an identity-provider session. Include in-flight
+   login completion and refresh paths so they cannot resurrect old sessions.
+4. Hosted deployment fit and an operating cost/ownership record for the pilot.
+   Confirm the selected flow requires no volunteer phone data in the provider.
+
+Then update this ADR with the decision, alternatives rejected, evidence, and date,
+and reassess FR-001 in ADD-001. No provider research, credentials, or integration
+evidence is claimed by this document.
+
+## Effect on readiness
+
+FR-001 is BLOCKED for epic definition because its actual sign-in journey is
+unresolved. FR-002 and FR-003 may be decomposed against the authenticated-account
+contract, and NFR-001 may be decomposed against the local session contract. Their
+end-to-end delivery still depends on the eventual provider integration. NFR-002
+and NFR-003 remain mandatory selection constraints, not reasons to waive D-01.

+# ADR-002 — Hosted modular monolith and transactional booking
+
+## Context and design decision
+
+The pilot has about 120 volunteers and a coordinator, and NFR-003 prohibits an
+on-site server dependency. Use a single hosted application and managed relational
+database. Separate identity/session, booking, and roster responsibilities in code.
+All application data access is server-side. Keep application instances stateless
+apart from shared authoritative database state.
+
+Use a database transaction and a per-shift lock for capacity checks and booking
+insertion, plus a unique volunteer/shift constraint for retries. Require every
+writer that can change availability to follow this protocol. Read roster data
+from the primary database to avoid replica lag after successful bookings.
+
+## Alternatives and consequences
+
+Microservices would add deployment and consistency boundaries without a stated
+need. Browser-to-database writes would expand the authorization surface. An
+eventually consistent booking queue would complicate the promise of booking an
+open shift. None is part of this design.
+
+The central database is an availability dependency; failures must be visible and
+must not produce false booking confirmations. Managed backups and a restore
+exercise are required before rollout. Select a hosting vendor/region and record
+retention and recovery settings during the foundation epic. This ADR chooses a
+deployment shape, not a purchased service, price, or availability guarantee.
+
+## Verification obligations
+
+Compete for the last place from separate transactions; assert no overbooking.
+Retry a committed request whose response was lost; assert one booking. Verify
+closed/past shifts reject new bookings and an empty day has a valid empty roster.
+Inspect deployment dependencies to show every runtime service is hosted. Verify
+backup restoration using synthetic data before the pilot.
+
+The architectural contract is sufficient for epic definition. Runtime evidence
+is NOT_RUN because no implementation is present. See
+[ADD-001](../add/ADD-001.md) for requirement-level dependencies and assumptions.

+# ADR-003 — Authoritative sessions and coordinator-only contact access
+
+## Context and design decision
+
+NFR-001 requires an administrator to revoke a volunteer's sessions within five
+minutes. NFR-002 allows only the coordinator to see volunteer phone numbers.
+Both are server-side, cross-cutting constraints.
+
+Issue an opaque local session secret in a protected cookie after verified sign-in;
+store only its hash, account ID, expiry, and account session generation. Every
+protected request reads authoritative state from the primary database and checks
+current roles. Never trust a browser-supplied role or a cached positive decision.
+
+An administrator revokes all existing sessions by atomically incrementing the
+target account's generation. Return success after commit and record a security
+audit event without secrets or contact values. Old session generations fail on
+every instance. Database failures deny protected access. Session refresh must
+revalidate the old session; it must never update an old session to a new generation.
+
+At sign-in initiation, associate the attempt with the current local account
+generation when known; otherwise retain its server-side initiation time and check
+against the account's latest revocation time at completion. Store that revocation
+time alongside generation. Serialize session issuance and revocation on the
+account row so a concurrent callback cannot create a fresh valid session from a
+pre-revocation attempt. Fresh authentication initiated after revocation may create
+a new session; permanent account suspension is a separate policy.
+
+Enforce a 60-second maximum protected-request lifetime, including database work,
+so work admitted before revocation cannot continue past the five-minute bound.
+The implementation must demonstrate actual cancellation, not merely a proxy
+timeout while backend work continues. No protected background streams are planned.
+
+Store phone contacts separately from general account data. Only a coordinator
+authorization check permits the contact query and projection. A volunteer cannot
+read their own stored phone through this product; an administrator needs the
+coordinator role to read any phone. An account with both roles is authorized by
+its coordinator role. Use `no-store` responses and omit phone values from logs,
+traces, analytics, exceptions, and nonproduction fixtures.
+
+## Alternatives and consequences
+
+Provider logout alone would tie the five-minute promise to an unselected external
+service. Long-lived self-contained application tokens without an authoritative
+revocation check would not implement this design. Checking the database on each
+request costs a query and makes it an access-availability dependency; that is an
+explicit tradeoff at this pilot's scale.
+
+UI-only phone hiding still exposes the API payload and is rejected. Application
+administration must not imply contact access. Infrastructure maintenance access
+is separate from product roles: restrict and audit privileged database/backup
+access, and do not offer raw contact browsing through routine support tooling.
+
+## Verification obligations
+
+Revoke two active browser sessions; replay each against every protected route
+immediately and at/after five minutes. Include session refresh, concurrent login
+callbacks, multiple app instances, database outage, and slow in-flight requests.
+Prove that unauthorized revocation fails and successful revocation is audited.
+
+Exercise anonymous, volunteer, administrator-only, coordinator, and combined-role
+accounts. Inspect raw API responses, server-rendered HTML, errors, caches, and
+telemetry for a synthetic phone marker. Only coordinator-authorized contact
+responses may contain it. Verify role removal takes effect at the next request.
+
+These obligations are ready to become epic acceptance criteria. Their runtime
+status is NOT_RUN; the selected-provider cases depend on ADR-001.
